title: UAE Free Zone vs Mainland Company: Which Setup Is Better for You?
description: Compare UAE free zone and mainland company formation: ownership, trading rights, licences, visas, costs, corporate tax and which one suits your business model.
lead: Compare UAE free zone and mainland company formation: ownership, trading rights, licences, visas, costs, corporate tax and which one suits your business model.
body:
One of the first decisions when setting up a company in the UAE is whether to choose a free zone or the mainland. Both are legitimate and popular, but they serve different business models.

Free zone company

Free zones such as DMCC, JAFZA, IFZA, Meydan, RAKEZ and others offer simplified set-up, flexible office options and a range of licence packages. - Up to 100 percent foreign ownership - Fast incorporation and straightforward documentation - Possible corporate tax advantages for qualifying activities - Restrictions on trading directly with the UAE mainland unless allowed by the zone and licence

Mainland company

A mainland LLC is licensed by the Department of Economic Development (DED) of the relevant emirate. - Freedom to trade across the UAE and bid for government work - Most activities now allow 100 percent foreign ownership, though some regulated activities need approvals or a local partner - A physical office or lease is generally required - Normal 9 percent corporate tax regime applies

How to choose

  1. Who are your customers: mainland clients or international buyers?
  2. Do you need retail premises or a large team?
  3. How many visas do you need?
  4. What is your budget for licence, office and renewals?
  5. Which activity will appear on the licence?

Common mistakes

  • Choosing a free zone only because it is cheap, then discovering mainland restrictions
  • Ignoring corporate tax, VAT and audit obligations
  • Not planning bank-account opening and KYC early
